title: Pope's official prayer app commits cardinal sin, leaks 700K+ users' info
content_html:
REG AD

Security

(Security) hole-ier than thou

Click To Pray, a prayer app endorsed by the Pope with hundreds of thousands of users worldwide, has leaked people’s names and email addresses for months - or longer - according to an ethical hacker who said she found and reported the security vulnerability six months ago to no avail. This app needs to take a vow of silence when it comes to your personal information.

The app, available in seven languages and on iOS, Android, and clicktopray.org, is the official app of the Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network. It connects users across the globe to pray for the Holy Father’s intentions, and as of July 2026, it has 719,517 registered accounts.

It’s also very leaky, according to security sleuth BobDaHacker, who says she spotted and disclosed the vulnerability to the Pope’s Worldwide Prayer Network on January 3.

REG AD

“The vulnerability is still live,” the hacker said in a Friday blog. “Nobody has ever responded. I guess my email wasn't in their prayers."

REG AD

The Reg readers likely remember BobDaHacker for her previous research exposing a free-food flaw in McDonald's ordering system and open controls on Chinese robot manufacturer Pudu Robotics.

This latest security hole stems from an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) bug in the prayer app. This is a very common and easy-to-exploit type of flaw that occurs when a website or an app blindly accepts user-provided input to view or modify resources without checking to see if the user is actually authorized to retrieve the data.

“You ask for your own data, the server gives it to you,” BobDaHacker explains. “You ask for someone else's data, the server gives you that too. Thou shalt not authorize, apparently.”

When you sign up for a Click To Pray account, the app assigns you a sequential numeric user ID. As BobDaHacker uncovered, the API endpoint GET https://api[.]clicktopray.org/user/users/{id} will return user data for any account - not just your own account - so long as you supply a valid, five-digit user ID. 

It doesn’t perform any authorization check or ownership validation. “Just increment the number and get someone else's data,” she wrote.

This data includes users’ email addresses, first and last names, country, dates of birth, and whether the account has been deleted, and the API exposes all 719,517 accounts on the prayer site. “With sequential user IDs and no rate limiting, an attacker could enumerate every single account on the platform,” the hacker explained. “One GET request per user. for i in range(1, 719518): scrape(). That's it. That's the exploit.”

As BobDaHacker points out, many of these users are likely older individuals, not all that tech savvy, and very trusting of anything Vatican related, making these exposed accounts a “phishing goldmine.”

“Imagine getting an email that says ‘The Holy Father requests your urgent attention’ with a Vatican-looking link,” she wrote. “Grandma is clicking that. Every time.”

REG AD

And then it gets even worse.

The signup endpoint, POST https://api.clicktopray.org/user/users/sign-up, returns the account's validation_hash directly in the response body, and that value is the same UUID used in the email verification link. This means someone could sign up using any email address and verify the account before the confirmation message reached the inbox.

Plus, BobDaHacker’s email client flagged the real verification email with a warning that it had failed the domain’s authentication requirements and might have been spoofed or improperly forwarded.

“So not only is the API leaking 700,000 email addresses that could be used for phishing, but the real emails from Click To Pray already look like phishing,” the hacker noted. “An attacker wouldn't even need to try hard. They could send a pixel-perfect phishing email and it would have the same level of email authentication as the real thing: none. God works in mysterious ways.”

The Register reached out to the Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network and did not receive any response. BobDaHacker says she’s still praying for one, too.®

content_html_zh:
REG AD

安全

（安全）比你更漏洞

据一名道德黑客称，Click To Pray 是一款得到教皇认可、在全球拥有数十万用户的祈祷应用程序，该应用程序已泄露人们的姓名和电子邮件地址数月甚至更长时间。她表示，她在六个月前发现并报告了该安全漏洞，但毫无效果。 当涉及到您的个人信息时，这个应用程序需要发誓保持沉默。

该应用程序有七种语言版本，可在 iOS、Android 和 clicktoray.org 上使用，是教皇全球祈祷网络的官方应用程序。 它连接全球用户为教宗的意图祈祷，截至 2026 年 7 月，它拥有 719,517 个注册帐户。

据安全侦探 BobDaHacker 称，该漏洞的漏洞也非常严重，她于 1 月 3 日发现了该漏洞，并向教皇全球祈祷网络披露了该漏洞。

REG AD

“该漏洞仍然存在，”黑客在周五的博客中表示。 “没有人回应过。 我猜我的电子邮件不在他们的祈祷之列。”

REG AD

《Reg》的读者可能还记得 BobDaHacker 之前的研究，该研究揭露了麦当劳点餐系统中的免费食品缺陷以及对中国机器人制造商 Pudu Robotics 的开放控制。

这个最新的安全漏洞源于祈祷应用程序中的不安全直接对象引用（IDOR）错误。 这是一种非常常见且易于利用的缺陷，当网站或应用程序盲目接受用户提供的输入来查看或修改资源而不检查用户是否确实有权检索数据时，就会发生这种缺陷。

“你要求自己的数据，服务器就会给你，”BobDaHacker 解释道。 “你要求别人提供数据，服务器也会给你。 显然，你不应该授权。”

当您注册“Click To Pray”帐户时，应用程序会为您分配一个连续的数字用户 ID。 正如 BobDaHacker 所发现的那样，只要您提供有效的五位数用户 ID，API 端点 GET https://api[.]clicktoray.org/user/users/{id} 将返回任何帐户的用户数据，而不仅仅是您自己的帐户。

它不执行任何授权检查或所有权验证。 “只需增加数字并获取其他人的数据，”她写道。

这些数据包括用户的电子邮件地址、名字和姓氏、国家/地区、出生日期以及帐户是否已被删除，并且 API 公开了祈祷网站上的所有 719,517 个帐户。 “通过连续的用户 ID 并且没有速率限制，攻击者可以枚举平台上的每个帐户，”黑客解释道。 “每个用户一个 GET 请求。 对于范围内的 i(1, 719518)：scrape()。 就是这样。 这就是漏洞。”

正如 BobDaHacker 指出的那样，这些用户中的许多人可能是老年人，不太懂技术，并且非常信任与梵蒂冈相关的任何东西，这使得这些暴露的帐户成为“网络钓鱼金矿”。

“想象一下，收到一封电子邮件，上面写着‘教宗请求您紧急关注’，并带有一个看起来像梵蒂冈的链接，”她写道。 “奶奶正在点击那个。 每次。”

REG AD

然后情况会变得更糟。

注册端点 POST https://api.clicktopray.org/user/users/sign-up 直接在响应正文中返回帐户的validation_hash，该值与电子邮件验证链接中使用的 UUID 相同。 这意味着有人可以使用任何电子邮件地址注册并在确认消息到达收件箱之前验证帐户。

此外，BobDaHacker 的电子邮件客户端标记了真实的验证电子邮件，并警告该电子邮件未满足域的身份验证要求，并且可能已被欺骗或不当转发。

“因此，API 不仅泄露了 700,000 个可用于网络钓鱼的电子邮件地址，而且来自 Click To Pray 的真实电子邮件看起来也像是网络钓鱼，”黑客指出。 “攻击者甚至不需要努力。 他们可以发送像素完美的网络钓鱼电子邮件，并且它具有与真实邮件相同级别的电子邮件身份验证：没有。 上帝以神秘的方式工作。”

《纪事报》联系了教皇的全球祈祷网络，但没有收到任何回复。 BobDaHacker 说她还在为一个人祈祷。®
